key_insight: Symbolic regression discovers analytically tractable approximations that substantially improve accuracy across three polymer statistical mechanics problems.
engineering_relevance: More accurate closed-form expressions could improve polymer constitutive models while preserving analytical tractability.
method: Use reinforcement-learning-based Deep Symbolic Optimization and genetic-programming-based PyOperon.
Fit expressions for WLC force–extension, ln(n!), and FJC radial probability density.
Apply residual learning, including physics-informed residuals for the FJC model.
evidence_signal: Reported maximum relative errors for WLC are below 0.15% with DSO and 0.05% with PyOperon; approximation improvements reach 13,000-fold for ln(n!) on n ∈ [1, 30] and 11.2-fold over Darabi et al. for FJC density.
watch_item: Accuracy outside the evaluated ranges and robustness when embedded in engineering simulations require further validation.
paper_title: New Closed-Form Approximations in Statistical Mechanics Obtained by Symbolic Regression
